mprNumbering.Description: Adding numbering to the specified parameter of elements with the possibility of numbering in the schedules
mprNumbering.FullDescription: When working in a non-schedule view, you can specify the direction of numbering based on the arrangement of elements, or add numbering in the order in which elements were created. When working in a schedule, the plugin adds numbering in the order of items in the schedule (taking into account sorting). It is possible to set the prefix and suffix for the number

mprNumbering.t1: The work of the plugin is possible only in the schedule in the sorting settings of which the property "Itemize every instance" is checked
mprNumbering.t3: Standard frame selection – selection of elements in the current view with a frame with confirmation of the selection by pressing the "Finish" button. With this option, the numbering direction has nine options – in the order of creation and by the position of the elements.
mprNumbering.t4: Ordinal selection – selects each element for numbering in the order in which the numbering will be performed. With this option, the direction of numbering can be ascending or descending. Completion of the selection is invoked by pressing the Esc key.
mprNumbering.t5: Curve intersection – Select a curve (model line or detail line). The elements for numbering will be selected by finding the intersection of the curve with the geometry of the elements in the current view, projected onto the plane of the view. With this option, the direction of numbering can be ascending or descending.
mprNumbering.t6: It is possible to apply a filter by category and/or parameters to all element selections.
mprNumbering.t7: The list of parameters is filled in after selecting the elements for numbering.
mprNumbering.t12: The initial value can be a fractional value. A point or comma can be used to separate the integer part from the fractional part. The specified separator will be used when setting values in the text parameter. If the target parameter is of data type "Number", the specified separator will not affect the displayed result. If the target parameter is of data type "Integer", the numbering result will be converted to an integer by discarding the fractional part.
mprNumbering.t13: Leading zeros can be added to the initial value. For example, if the initial value is "01", and the step is "5", then the numbering result will be "01, 05, 10, 15...". Initial zeros are only taken into account if the target parameter has a string data type.
mprNumbering.t14: The geometric direction of numbering is calculated by the absolute values of X and Y of the element placement points. For linear objects the middle point is taken
mprNumbering.t15: When sorting linear objects, the center point is used. When sorting viewports, the center of the viewport is used. When sorting tags, the header placement point is used. In other cases, the insertion point of the element is used
mprNumbering.t16: You can apply letter numbering. To do this, specify the letter of the alphabet from which the alphabetic numbering will start as the initial value. Alphabetic numbering will be performed in the same case in which the initial value is specified.
mprNumbering.t17: Grouping by parameter is available only in schedules with the "Itemize every instance" option checked in the sorting settings
mprNumbering.t18: The option is available only in schedules that display information about model elements, i.e. in schedules where rows (elements) can be selected.
mprNumbering.t19: When the option is enabled, only the elements of the selected rows are numbered. If no rows are selected in the schedule, all elements are numbered
mprNumbering.t20: With rectangle selection and order selection, only nested families can be selected. Only shared nested families are separate model elements
mprNumbering.t21: Along route – select the start element of a pipe, duct, cable tray or conduit run. Elements for numbering are found by following the run through its connections from the selected element to its end. If the run has branches, you can number the longest path or the path to a specified element. With this option, the numbering direction can be ascending or descending
mprNumbering.t22: A mask is text in which the number parts are written in curly braces as their initial values. For example, the mask {1}.{1}.{1} gives the numbers 1.1.1, 1.1.2 and so on. A part is written with digits only or letters only. Leading zeros set the number length: the part {01} gives 01, 02 … 10. A letter part is numbered in the selected alphabet in the case of its initial value. A mask can contain up to five parts. A composite number can be written only to a text parameter
mprNumbering.t23: Step – how much the part increases with each change. Limit – the largest value of the part: after it, the part starts again from its initial value. If you set a limit for the first part, the numbers will start repeating after it. "With each number" – the part increases for each next number. "After limit on the right" – the part increases only when the next part goes past its limit. The last part always changes with each number
mprNumbering.t24: Groups are formed by the fields that have a header, footer or blank line enabled on the "Sorting/Grouping" tab of the schedule properties. Numbering is performed in each group of the last level. Fields that are used only for sorting do not form groups
mprNumbering.t25: Elements are additionally sorted by the specified parameters as the next levels after the schedule sorting. If the target parameter is used in the schedule sorting, the specified parameters are applied before it, and the new order will be visible in the schedule after numbering. Text is compared taking numbers into account: "2" comes before "10"
mprNumbering.t26: Additional sorting is available only in schedules with the "Itemize every instance" option checked in the sorting settings
mprNumbering.t27: The setting applies if the selected curve is a spline. For other curves, the intersection is always searched with the curve itself
mprNumbering.t28: Spline only – the intersection is searched with the spline itself (dashed line in the picture)
mprNumbering.t29: Control points – the intersection is searched with the polyline passing through the spline control points (solid lines in the picture). The spline itself is not taken into account
mprNumbering.t30: Spline and control points – the intersection is searched with both the spline and the polyline through the control points. An element crossing both lines is numbered once – by the intersection closer to the start of the spline
mprNumbering.t31: The numbering order is determined by the position of the intersection from the start to the end of the spline. An intersection with the polyline is converted to the corresponding position on the spline: the polyline segment between two control points corresponds to the part of the spline whose shape these points define
mprNumbering.t32: "Type Name" and "Family Name" are not Revit parameters. Numbering into them is performed by renaming the type or family the element belongs to. All instances of this type or family in the project get the new name, and the change affects tags, schedules and filters that use the name.
mprNumbering.t33: The name belongs to the type or family, not to the instance. Therefore types (families) are numbered in the order in which their first element appears, and the other elements of the same type (family) are skipped and do not take numbers.
mprNumbering.t34: Names must be unique: a type name within its family, a family name within the project. If the new name is already used by an object that is not being numbered, or is given to another numbered object (for example, with the "One number per group" option), the object is not renamed and is added to the report. A name cannot contain the characters \ : { } [ ] | ; < > ? ` ~.
mprNumbering.t35: The name is completely replaced by the number with the prefix and suffix. To keep the original name, take the prefix and suffix from a parameter and select the parameter with the type or family name for the suffix or prefix. When numbering again, the number is added to the already numbered name.
mprNumbering.t36: A family name can be changed only for loadable families and in-place families – elements of system families (walls, floors, pipes, etc.) are skipped. Clearing is not available for the type name and family name. Renaming can be undone with the Revit "Undo" command
